subject: Unexpected May invoice spike — suspected duplicate embed counts / provisional hold
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@brightcart.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com, accounts@brightcart.com
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected May invoice spike — can you explain?

Hi Jonas,

We just received our May invoice and there's a ~4.1x increase in embed/unit charges compared to April (see attached billing_snapshot_May2028.xlsx). That doesn't line up with our internal usage graphs — we had a small marketing test and one larger batch, but nothing near this.

Can you provide a line-item breakdown for the embed counts on invoice_202805.pdf? Also, our procurement team needs confirmation on whether the EU reverse-charge applies here; we submitted the VAT form in April. If reverse-charge does apply, we need to remit net of VAT.

We're asking for a provisional collection hold on the disputed amount while you investigate — can you advise next steps and an ETA?

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor

liam@brightcart.com

Date: 2028-06-01T12:05:00Z

Hi Liam — thanks for flagging this and sharing the snapshot. I'm escalating to Billing and Tax (cc'd).

Immediate next steps:
- Marissa (Billing Ops) will pull a detailed usage export for May and do a request-id level reconciliation.

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Liam O'Connor <liam@brightcart.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-01T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected May invoice spike — can you explain? (forensic snapshot attached)

On Thu, Jun 1, 2028 at 09:12 AM Liam O'Connor <liam@brightcart.com> wrote:
> We just received our May invoice and there's a ~4.1x increase in embed/unit charges compared to April...

Hi all — brief technical summary from Billing Ops after an initial pass. Full forensic export attached (usage_export_202805.csv). Key findings so far:

1) Evidence of high-volume duplicate embed calls tied to two API keys that were both live during the same window (2028-05-18 02:00 UTC — 2028-05-19 06:00 UTC). One key is your production key, the other appears to be a stale staging key that mirrored requests (likely a CI job).
2) The duplicate calls are exact matches on request_id and payload in ~87% of the flagged rows, which indicates client-side duplication rather than our server-side deduplication failure.
3) The invoice calculation used per-unit counts from final aggregation; duplicates were not collapsed because they appeared as separate requests in the logs.

Proposed immediate remediation:
- We can issue a provisional credit for the duplicated portion equal to 65% of the disputed embed charge while we complete the full audit (we typically set conservative provisional credits until root cause proof is complete).
- Collections hold: I've asked Collections to prevent collection activity on the disputed amount for 14 days to allow the audit and any contract amendment to be signed.
- Tax: Kimberly to confirm whether reverse-charge was applied on the original invoice; if not, we'll reissue a net invoice after the credit.

I've attached (usage_export_202805.csv) and invoice_202805.pdf for transparency. If BrightCart wants us to proceed faster we can increase provisional credit to 100% pending forensics, but we need explicit approval from your finance owner.

Next steps for BrightCart:
- Confirm PO/reference (attach the PO) and whether you approve a 100% provisional credit or prefer the standard 65% provisional.
- Confirm whether you want the reissued invoice net of VAT once tax confirms reverse-charge.

Happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: usage_export_202805.csv, invoice_202805.pdf

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@brightcart.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com, accounts@brightcart.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-02T08:44:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected May invoice spike — can you explain?

Hi Marissa / Jonas — thanks for the quick investigation and for the provisional hold.

We found the CI job that accidentally pointed the staging key at production during the May window; apologies on our side. Our finance team requires a signed amendment/credit note before we process a revised payment. I've attached our PO_7845.pdf and the procurement contact (procurement@brightcart.com) is on copy.

Please proceed with the 100% provisional credit to avoid operational disruption on our side; we'll sign the amendment and return it via DocuSign. Also confirm that the reissued invoice will be net of VAT under EU reverse-charge once Kimberly confirms the tax position.

Appreciate the help — a quick 20-minute call to confirm the docs would be great. I'm available today at 14:00-16:00 BST.

Cheers,
Liam

Attachment: PO_7845.pdf
